audit.why: EVEN at 5.5/10 fits 48.81% over 1260 games: Irelia owns levels 1-3 against a no-escape-yet Vladimir, the lane levels out once Sanguine Pool is ranked, and Vladimir out-scales into teamfights through Crimson Pact health-to-AP and Hemoplague.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0] and early both claimed Vladimir has no Sanguine Pool before level 6. Sanguine Pool is his W, not his ultimate.
audit.why: It is a level-2-available ability on a 28s cooldown at rank 1; the real early window is its downtime, not a level gate.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten around the 28s rank-1 cooldown. Level 6 spike rewritten to Hemoplague (flat 120s, amplifies damage taken, heals per champion hit). First item spike is Grievous Wounds timing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two applicable interactions were absent: Sanguine Pool's 2s of untargetability eats a full commit, and Vladimir's Transfusion/Hemoplague healing makes Grievous Wounds timing decide extended trades.
audit.why: Both are the decisive mechanics and neither reached the page; anti-heal appeared only in report[8].
audit.corrected: Untargetable window written into breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[2].d; anti-heal written into ahead, phases[5].why and whys[5].

audit.why: It is the field that carries real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Sanguine Pool 28s to 16s, Transfusion 9s to 4.6s at no mana cost, Hemoplague flat 120s.

edits.before: Reset-dance the wave into his face: four stacks, E-stun, Q the kill threat. The lane is a minion-count quiz.
edits.after: Skill window: Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1 — go while it is spent; a whiffed dash feeds his Transfusion.

edits.before: Vanguard's Edge online — the all-in caps with a wall of disengage-proof marks. Dive with the wave as your fuel.
edits.after: Hemoplague amplifies your damage taken for its whole duration and heals him per champion hit — trade before it lands.

edits.before: First item spike: stacked trades delete mages and your sustain mocks their poke math.
edits.after: First item: Grievous Wounds decides it — without anti-heal Transfusion refunds your combo.

edits.before: Late Irelia surfs the fight: Q-reset through their line, stun the carry pair, and shred whoever peels.
edits.after: Late he stacks health into AP off Crimson Pact and Hemoplague swings fights — you need him alone in a side lane.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 hold as your dive still outpaces his poke-only kit pre-6
edits.after: Levels 4-5 turn on whether Sanguine Pool is up when you commit

edits.before: Pool lets him escape once, but baiting it first still gives you the win on the real engage
edits.after: Hemoplague amplifies the damage you take and heals him for every champion it hits

edits.before: First item burst kills him before his HP-scaling kit and Hemoplague matter
edits.after: Without Grievous Wounds, Transfusion simply refunds whatever you land

edits.before: Late-game HP-stack Vlad poke is real, but decisive short all-ins keep this favor yours
edits.after: Crimson Pact turns his health items into AP, and he answers dives untargetable

edits.before: No Sanguine Pool yet means your early all-ins land clean, favour is yours
edits.after: Sanguine Pool at 28s means your early all-ins land clean on its downtime

edits.before: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Defiant Dance has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Sanguine Pool (W) is 28s at rank 1 and 16s at rank 5, and 2s of untargetable eats a full commit — bait it, then go. - Transfusion (Q) drops from 9s to 4.6s at rank 5 and costs no mana: assume it is up every trade. - Hemoplague (R) is a flat 120s.

edits.before: Q-reset through two low minions onto his chest, four-stack autos, E-stun the retreat — the wave-funded all-in he budgeted zero for.
edits.after: Bladesurge (Q) and Flawless Duet (E) each stack the passive; arrive at four before you touch him, or bonus on-hit damage never funds the kill.

edits.before: Dashing in under-stacked with W down — Irelia without the engine is a melee minion with a famous haircut.
edits.after: Every low minion is a Bladesurge charge; shove them under his tower and he pools away with no dash targets left.

edits.before: Vladimir whiffs Sanguine Pool and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Pool is 28s at rank 1 — whiff it and he is yours for that window.

edits.before: Vladimir wins by landing Sanguine Pool, denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Vladimir wins by pooling out your commit, healing it back with Transfusion, and stacking health into free AP.

edits.before: Carry through the dance — the wave funds dives no cooldown can, and your R turns skirmishes into no-exit interviews.
edits.after: Carry by catching him mid-pool cooldown: 28s at rank 1 is long enough for four stacks, a stun and a full reset chain.

edits.before: Ahead, dance louder: crash waves into Vladimir's face, stun the answers, and surf resets through every river fight.
edits.after: Ahead, buy Grievous Wounds early: his health-into-AP scaling only pays off if Transfusion keeps refunding your damage.

edits.before: Before Vlad hits level 6 he has no Sanguine Pool escape, so once you have Q-E you can all-in through his Transfusion poke and punish him hard.
edits.after: Until Sanguine Pool is ranked up it is 28s down, so once you have Bladesurge and Flawless Duet, all-in on that cooldown and stun the retreat.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 favor you clearly — Vlad has no pool yet, so every all-in where you close the gap with Bladesurge wins outright since his only tool is Transfusion poke.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 favor you clearly — Transfusion is his only trade at 9s and no mana cost, so close with Bladesurge off a low minion and out-trade him with stacks.

notes: Sanguine Pool is Vladimir's W, not a level-6 unlock; two content fields asserted he has no pool before 6. Fixed. Riot's Tides of Blood text says it 'can be blocked by enemy units' — that phrasing is not clear enough to build advice on for a melee opponent, so no claim about minion-blocking his E was written. Cross-layer chart disagreement on four of seven rows was corrected by moving win[] to match the existing phases[].side values and rewriting all four whys.
